Investment Snapshot

Brick Shell, Blank Canvas

The heavy lifting on a building like this is usually the envelope — and here the brick, roof, and windows are holding up well. The money goes inside: ceilings, finishes, kitchens, baths, and heat. That's a cleaner value-add real estate play than most multifamily investment deals at this size in Northwest Indiana.

Rehab Scope

$150K–$200K Interior Plan

Walking it room by room: the ceilings are opened up in several rooms with joists exposed, wall finishes are failing, and kitchens and baths are dated or partly demoed. Radiators, panels, and water heating are in place but need to be checked. Outside, the brick is in good shape with no major deterioration.

Where the Budget Gets Efficient

  • Envelope is sound: brick exterior in good shape and no known active roof leaks — no tear-off or tuckpointing budget built in
  • Baseboard heat: the best affordable heating upgrade for this building — lower cost than a new boiler or ducted HVAC, and it allows per-unit control
  • No system-wide issues reported on electrical or plumbing — budgeted as an allowance, not a full replacement
  • Repeatable layouts: four similar units let you buy finishes in bulk
Preliminary allocation, not a contractor quote. Assumes no major structural work or full mechanical replacement, and excludes extra garage-studio scope beyond the assumed building area.
Exit Strategies

Four Ways to Run It

Rental property investments with more than one income path, depending on how you want to operate it.

01

Long-Term Rentals

Four independent units plus the studio if permitted. Separate utilities, in-unit laundry, and updated kitchens and baths boost marketability.

02

Rent-By-Room

The 16-bedroom layout supports higher gross revenue. Bath count, shared space, fire protection, and permitted occupancy drive the model.

03

Section 8 / Vouchers

Housing Choice Voucher participation is possible, subject to unit eligibility, inspection, payment standards, and approval.

04

Mid-Term Rentals

An alternative for workforce or contract tenants. Conventional rentals stay the more supportable baseline.
